title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Bill. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Bill
options.lineage: 1960s-70s gig handbills & KL risograph show posters
options.thesis: The whole site as one printed show bill for the stadium: every Section a line on the bill, its view the plate.
options.viewport: A bill masthead ruled across the top, the selected Section's view as the big halftone plate, and the 104 Sections as a ruled numbered column.
options.risk: Display type on an Operate surface: if the bill voice leaks into numbers and labels, the site stops being scannable.

raised.raise: State is line form before hue: empty, photographed, and selected Sections differ by rule weight, dash, and doubling, so the bill reads in greyscale.
One continuous sheet: the whole surface is a single printed page, never a mosaic of floating rounded cards, so nothing drifts off the bill.
The selected Section swells forward in scale and ink while the rest recede, a depth cue that needs no motion.

options.label: The Ticket Stub
options.thesis: Every Section read as its ticket stub, the view as what the stub saw.
options.viewport: A stub masthead of Section, Row and Seat fields, with the view plate tearing off below it.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on: familiar and effective, but not out of distribution.

options.label: Concourse Split-Flap Board
options.lineage: airport and train split-flap departure boards
options.thesis: The stadium board: Sections as ruled rows that flip to the selected view.
options.viewport: A fixed grid of ruled rows with the open Section flipping to its photo.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: Sections map to fixed rows and columns. Loses narrowly on audience fit - the fan is at a gig, not at a gate.
options.risk: Reads as transit cosplay when the flap motion is decorative.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: The concert's own light: content stacked in horizon bands from blackout to day.
options.viewport: A low cobalt horizon band under a dark sky, the view emerging into daylight.
options.case: Holds the concert world strongly; the atmosphere band competes with the metadata, so product clarity loses a step.
options.risk: Atmospheric banding can bury the data a fan came for.

options.label: Man-Machine Grid
options.thesis: Every Section a node wired on one strict modular grid.
options.viewport: A tight modular grid with orthogonal connectors running from Section numbers to their plates.
options.case: Keeps product clarity with a diagram-native layout; audience identification is generic-retro rather than gig-specific.
options.risk: Reads as a synth album cover if the grid is not strict.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.case: Fuses poorly: a spectrogram is not a fan's world.
options.kept: State as line form rather than colour.

options.label: Orizuru Sequence
options.case: Fuses poorly: folding steps do not carry a browse-and-compare task.
options.kept: One continuous sheet with no floating cards.

options.label: Console Void
options.case: Fuses poorly: game-console atmosphere is not the ticket-decision scene.
options.kept: The selected object swells forward, the rest recede.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: The expected thing, executed impeccably: a search box, a photo grid, and a seat map.
canonCard.viewport: Search first, then a photo grid, then a seat map, at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
